<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57c51aab4d2f63293676e9412daed8a5fc54c1bc` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1ec98eb918dd27e41aed94ca58f2bc395a8e9e29` — the merge of head `023da3b2d48ccb56351bbbbf103aec7e5140e5cb` into base `57c51aab4d2f63293676e9412daed8a5fc54c1bc`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1ec98eb918dd27e41aed94ca58f2bc395a8e9e29 && git checkout 1ec98eb918dd27e41aed94ca58f2bc395a8e9e29
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 57c51aab4d2f63293676e9412daed8a5fc54c1bc 023da3b2d48ccb56351bbbbf103aec7e5140e5cb && git checkout -B drift-repro 57c51aab4d2f63293676e9412daed8a5fc54c1bc && git merge --no-ff 023da3b2d48ccb56351bbbbf103aec7e5140e5cb

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57c51aab4d2f63293676e9412daed8a5fc54c1bc
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 57c51aab4d2f63293676e9412daed8a5fc54c1bc` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

The premise was re-read on `origin/main`: `summaryOperations.field` is `z.string()` there, so a count without it is refused as the card describes.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set, metadata door: `summaryOperations: { object, function: 'count' }` with no `field` is now accepted at `FieldSchema` and therefore at every embedding (`data/Object`, `data/ObjectExtension`, `system/AddFieldOperation`, the 14 ledger sites). RIGHT: this is what the card asked and what the describe always said. A count that carries `field` stays accepted and ignored (engine reads none for count). RIGHT, and no stored row changes meaning.
- Accept set, every other function: `sum`/`min`/`max`/`avg` without `field` is still refused, now by a `custom` issue at `['summaryOperations','field']` with a prescription naming the function and the `count` alternative, instead of `invalid_type`. RIGHT: same refusal set, better message; the path is unchanged so Studio's `objectFieldLocator` (`fields.NAME.summaryOperations.field`) still lands it on the inspector. Zod 4 skips object-level checks when the base parse is aborted, so a missing or invalid `function` yields its own `invalid_type` and no second issue from the refinement, consistent with the head's exactly-one-issue tests.
- Public TS surface of `@objectstack/spec/data`: one new export, `summaryFunctionReadsField(fn)`; `api-surface/data.json` and `export-origins/data.json` carry it. RIGHT as an additive export; under ruling A (2026-10-21) a TS export alone does not set the level.
- Public TS type of `@objectstack/objectql`: `SummaryDescriptor.sourceField` becomes optional. RIGHT: it is what `buildSummaryIndex` already stored for a field-less count; `aggregateSummaryValue` sends no `field` for count and the batch accumulator reads `row[sourceField]` only when `fn !== 'count'`, now guarded for `undefined`. The one other `sourceField` reader in `packages/objectql/src` is the guarded line itself.
- Published JSON Schema: `field` leaves `required` on every embedding; the value-conditional rule is dropped (no projectable arm states an if/then: the closed list in `refinement-projection.ts` is required-one-of, non-blank-string, dependent-required (presence-only), banned-keys, banned-key-pattern), so `summaryOperations` is recorded at 14 sites in `dropped-refinements.baseline.json`, 892 to 906, with the schema count unchanged at 244. RIGHT and honest; `check:generated`, `check:strictness-ledger`, `check:authorable-surface` are green on the head.
- Metadata forms (`field.form.ts`, `object.form.ts`): the `field` sub-row drops `required: true`. RIGHT, and the only expressible option: the metadata-form row schema (`view.zod.ts:3586`) has `required: z.boolean().optional()` and no conditional row attribute, so "required unless count" cannot be stated in the form; the door refuses a field-less sum one seam later with the prescription. Help text unchanged, so the generated translation bundles do not move (`check:generated` green).
- Studio editor: `SummaryConfigFields` reads the same predicate; no child-field control for count, the note replaces the old "still required, pick any child field" copy (en/zh). RIGHT: one rule, two readers, as the seat ruling asked ("not Studio fills an arbitrary field").
- `snapshotSummaryPlan.ts`: type guard for the now-optional key on a `sum`. RIGHT, no behaviour change.
- Lint `ROLLUP_NON_NUMERIC_AGGREGAND`: scoped to min/max and guarded by `typeof childFieldName === 'string'`. No change needed. RIGHT.
- Metadata-protocol kind: declared `none`. WRONG, see ②.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/27462-count-rollup-without-field.md`: `@objectstack/spec` patch, `@objectstack/objectql` patch, `@object-ui/app-shell` patch, `@object-ui/i18n` patch, with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` in both the PR body and the changeset body. The `Check Changeset` run and `check-changeset-no-major` are green, but that gate only checks the declared kind against the levels; which kind is right is this section's job.
- The kind is wrong. The WHICH LEVEL rule (`pr-automation.yml:757`, ruling A 2026-10-21 on #25105; AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3) sets the level by "the change to what a metadata author can write". This diff changes exactly that: an author can now write a count roll-up without `summaryOperations.field`, which every spec before this head refuses with 422 at the door. `none` is defined as "everything else: description or error text, non-authorable internal types, REST, drivers, services, the console"; a widened authorable accept set is none of those. The stated reason `added` takes `minor` ("an app that writes a new key must be able to name a minor floor") applies with more force here: an app that writes the newly accepted shape against an older spec is not silently stripped, it is refused. A requirement loosened is the mirror of "a requirement tightened" (`narrowed`), and the PR's own account calls it an accept-set widening.
- Must-fix (②-1): `Metadata-protocol: added` in the PR body and the changeset body, and `'@objectstack/spec': minor` (the moved package that carries the widening; the other three may stay `patch`). With a non-`none` kind the `Skills-docs:` line is owed for real (review-checklist.md L18), see ③/④.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right. `(widening)` adds no BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 disposition is owed; none is written. Right.
- Clause-②: yes (widening). The contract review is owed at this tier and this record is it.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none declared. Nothing to escalate.
- Deviation 1, `Skills-docs: none edited`, naming `field-types.md:259` and `relationships.md:201`: the two named lines are `sum` examples with `field: 'amount' // ignored for count` and stay true. The dev missed the row that spells the shape: `skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md:125` writes `summaryOperations ({ object, field, function, relationshipField?, filter? })`, marking `relationshipField` and `filter` optional and `field` not, which after this head teaches a requirement the spec no longer has. Under the declared `none` the line was not owed; under the corrected kind (②-1) it is, and `none edited` is false. Must-fix (③-1), folded into ②-1: spell `field?` at :125 with a word that a count omits it (or a one-line count example beside the sum one), and write `Skills-docs: updated here`.
- Deviation 2, ui vitest narrowed to the moved files and importers: discharged by the head's check-runs, Test UI 16/16 shards green and Type Check UI green.
- Deviation 3, an 18 KB probe file left at the dev container's root: outside the repo and the diff, nothing in the tree; no action here.
- Docs-drift bot (advisory): of the 12 hand-written pages it lists, the only one that restates this rule is `content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx`, and the diff moves it (table row and the count example drop `field: 'id'`); `import-mappings.mdx` is listed through an unrelated `sourceField`. The 2 release-owned pages are untouched. Right.
- Follow-up owed, should-fix (③-2): `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/studio-authoring.json`, item `studio-authoring.summary-field-authoring` (the card's own QA source), acceptance clause 3 reads "saved spec-valid: summaryOperations { object, field, function }" and its verify expects both summaries to carry "the authored object, field and function". On this head the count saves and reads back with no `field`, so the clause now scores a correct run as a failure. A checklist-author follow-up (revision 3: the count carries no `field`, the sum does), not a change on this PR.

### ④ Design judgment

**packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts** (against the seat ruling in 6492937618, the #27157 `refuseFixedCurrencyWithoutCode` precedent it cites, and its first consumers: the metadata door and `ObjectQL.buildSummaryIndex`)
- The rule lives once, `summaryFunctionReadsField`, and the refinement reads it; the message names the function and the fix. Matches the ruling's two halves: optional for count, required with a prescription for the rest, and Studio does not fill an arbitrary field.
- `.superRefine(refuseSummaryWithoutField)` sits on the `strictObject` node (a `closedObject`, a `ZodObject` subclass) before `.optional()`, so `FieldSchema.shape.summaryOperations` carries the check into `component.zod.ts:6736` and into objectui's `form.zod.ts:1170` (which walks and clones defs, checks included). Verified by reading, not by the PR body.
- Tried to break it: (a) `summaryOperations` absent: the optional short-circuits, no refinement. (b) `function` absent or not in the enum: the object parse is aborted, Zod 4 skips the check, one issue. (c) count with a stale `field`: accepted, engine ignores it (`aggregateSummaryValue` omits `field` for count; the accumulator never reads it for count). (d) a non-count descriptor with no field reaching the registry around the parse: the accumulator's new guard reads no value; `aggregateSummaryValue` would send `field: undefined`, which is the pre-existing behaviour for that already-refused shape, not widened here. (e) the `summaryField`/`targetField` aliases: strict-object suggestion vocabulary, refused as unknown keys as before. No finding.
- The published JSON Schema can no longer say "field required on a sum"; the ledger records it at every site and the door still refuses. This is the ADR-sanctioned disposition for a value-conditional rule. Should-fix, not blocking: none beyond ②.
- Finding: the one new public export is `summaryFunctionReadsField(fn: string | undefined)`, typed on `string` rather than the function enum. Acceptable: Studio feeds it `'' || undefined`, and the describe says an unset function answers `true`. No change asked.

**packages/spec/src/data/field.form.ts** and **packages/spec/src/data/object.form.ts** (against the schema they mirror and the metadata-form row schema at `view.zod.ts:3586`)
- Both sub-rows drop `required: true`, the comment in each points at the predicate. The row schema offers `required` as a plain boolean and no conditional form, so the alternative "required unless count" cannot be authored; dropping it is the design, and the help text "ignored for count" still tells the author which case needs it. `metadata-form-zod-reconciliation` and the declared-rows pin are unmoved and green. The reconciliation's `object.fields.summaryOperations` entry still describes the quick-add grid as capturing object / field / function, which is true as a control set. No finding.

**Governed skill surface (not in `hits`, read because the Skills-docs line claims it)**: `skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md:125` teaches `field` as a required member (see ③-1). Must-fix as part of ②-1.

Must-fix: ②-1 (kind `added`, spec `minor`, both declaration sites) with ③-1 (`field-types.md:125` and `Skills-docs: updated here`). Should-fix: ③-2 (checklist item revision, follow-up card). Everything else holds against the cited code.
